text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore among four countries launching landmark initiative to foster firmer international commitment to environmental issues.
- Singapore $10-million negligence suit against PowerGas Ltd over gas explosion at Ginza Plaza five years ago settled for S$9.4 million.

- U.S. stock prices slip off their lofty perch when comments by Japan's Prime Minister spook bond market and send interest rates higher. Dow Jones industrial average, which started Monday at record level, lost 192.25 points, second-biggest point drop ever.
- Singapore's financial institutions made a combined S$5.9 billion profit last year, 31.2 percent more than in 1995, Monetary Authority of Singapore Managing Director Lee Ek Tieng tells bankers.
- Trading on Singapore International Monetary Exchange will be expanded to include five futures and options contracts, following the signing of an agreement with DTB Deutsche Terminborse.
- Proposed bridge between Malaysia and Indonesia could start from Johor or Negri Sembilan instead of Malacca, Johor Chief Minister Datuk Abdul Ghani Othman says.

- Van Der Horst shares recovered slightly following reassurances from company that sharp profit drop in first-half was a "six-month blip" as election fever in Indonesia caused slowdown in its projects there.
- Wall Street steadied in morning trade on Tuesday after precipitous 192-point plunge on Monday.
- Thailand passes four "emergency" decrees to rescue ailing finance and property firms, with centrepiece that foreigners can now own majority stakes in Thai commercial banks and finance companies.
- Property Group First Capital Corp sells entire 13.14 percent stake in Sesdaq-listed retailer Heshe Holdings.
- Luxury watch retailer The Hour Glass posts better than expected second-half results due to turnaround in Swiss watch maker Gerald Genta.
- Mainboard-listed Econ International posts 49 percent rise in net profit to S$8.1 million for year ended March 31.
- Retail group Transmarco posts net loss of S$79,000 for financial year ending March 31 against S$1.1 million profit previously.
- CAM International Holdings sells industrial property at Kaki Bukit Techpark 1 for S$7.1 million.
- Computer education firm Informatics plans to extend franchise into Europe with recent purchase of UK accreditation agency, says senior company official.
